# mushroomdb

> The association engine for apps and AI agents. An embedded Rust graph database
> where edges are DECLARED, not inserted: you write rules, the db creates,
> maintains, and retracts edges automatically and can explain() why any edge exists.

## What it is

mushroomdb is a single-file-dependency embedded graph database for Rust, Python,
and TypeScript. Its differentiator is incremental linking rules: declare a predicate
once (cosine similarity, field equality, Jaccard overlap, FK match, geographic radius,
numeric range), and every subsequent write maintains the matching edges without any
manual bookkeeping. Edges are retracted automatically when properties diverge.

Primary audiences:
1. AI agents and coding assistants building association graphs and agent memory
   (built-in MCP server, explainable links, per-node history, hybrid search).
2. Small internal apps where relationships and matching are the product.

## Install / build

```sh
# Rust library (crates.io)
cargo add mushroomdb            # embedded GraphDb API
# Rust CLI + server (crates.io)
cargo install mushroomdb-cli    # `mushroomdb` binary: serve/query/demo/schema

# Python (from source until the PyPI wheel ships with the next release tag)
cd bindings/python
python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -U pip maturin
.venv/bin/maturin develop

# TypeScript client (from repo until the npm publish lands)
npm install /path/to/graph-db/clients/typescript
```

Docker (local build):
```sh
docker build -t mushroomdb:local .
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e MUSHROOMDB_TOKEN=secret mushroomdb:local
```

## Quick start (CLI)

```sh
mushroomdb demo ./db      # ingest demo graph (10 Orgs, 20 Projects, 30 People)
mushroomdb serve ./db     # HTTP server + UI at http://127.0.0.1:8080
mushroomdb mcp ./db       # stdio MCP JSON-RPC server for agent tools
```

## Key API (Rust)

```rust
use core_api::{GraphDb, RuleDef, Predicate};

let mut db = GraphDb::open(&path)?;

// Insert nodes
db.insert_node("Person", "alice", vec![
    ("skills".into(), Value::List(vec!["graph".into(), "rust".into()])),
    ("embedding".into(), Value::List(vec![0.9f64.into(), 0.2.into()])),
])?;

// Declare a rule — fires on every subsequent write
db.create_rule(RuleDef {
    name: "skill_fit".into(),
    src_label: "Person".into(),
    dst_label: "Org".into(),
    predicate: Predicate::Overlap { field: "skills".into(), min: 0.5 },
    edge_type: "FIT".into(),
    weight_prop: Some("score".into()),
    max_edges: Some(5),
    approximate: false,
})?;

// Cypher query
let rows = db.query("MATCH (p:Person)-[r:FIT]->(o:Org) RETURN p, o, r.score", &Default::default())?;

// Explain why an edge exists
let exps = db.explain("alice", "acme")?;  // [{rule, edge_type, weight, ...}]

// Per-node change history (WAL horizon since last snapshot)
let history = db.node_history("alice")?;

// Schema-as-code (idempotent apply)
let diff = db.apply_schema(&schema)?;  // SchemaDiff { created, updated, unchanged }

// Hybrid search (fulltext + vector via RRF)
let hits = db.search_hybrid("rust graph", "bio", Some(&embedding), "embedding", Some("Person"), 10)?;

// Subscribe to query results (incremental, allowlisted Cypher subset)
let sub = db.subscribe_query("MATCH (p:Person)-[:FIT]->(o:Org) RETURN p, o LIMIT 20")?;

// Node mask (ACL-scoped read)
let mask = NodeMask::from_keys(&db, ["alice", "bob"]);
let rows = db.query_masked("MATCH (p:Person) RETURN p", &Default::default(), &mask)?;
```

## MCP tools (16 total)

| Tool | Description |
|---|---|
| `query` | Cypher query; `mask` param for ACL-scoped read; `stub_hidden` bool for existence disclosure |
| `ingest_json` | Batch ingest nodes from JSON array |
| `create_rule` | Declare a derivation rule |
| `explain` | Explain rule-derived edges between two nodes |
| `explain_association` | Alias of explain; semantic name for agent workflows |
| `upsert_entity` | Insert or update a node by key (no existence check needed) |
| `find_similar` | (1) Vector search via HNSW; (2) edge-traversal neighbors |
| `hybrid_search` | RRF over fulltext + vector results |
| `neighborhood` | Multi-hop graph traversal |
| `node_info` | Node key, label, properties |
| `node_edges` | Incident edges with derived flag |
| `stats` | Live node/edge/rule counts |
| `node_history` | WAL change history for a node; returns {key, history, total_commits} |
| `edge_history` | Add/retract lifecycle for edges between two nodes with rule attribution; returns {a, b, events, total_commits} |
| `was_linked` | Point-in-time edge check; returns {linked} or error when outside horizon |
| `rename_node` | Rename a node's key; params: old_key, new_key; errors on absent old or duplicate new |

MCP is a trusted-local stdio interface — no bearer-token or role enforcement.
`stub_hidden` on the `query` tool applies to client-masked paths only; Cypher rows
are always omit-only.

Claude Desktop config:
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mushroomdb": {
      "command": "mushroomdb",
      "args": ["mcp", "/path/to/your/db"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Six predicate kinds

| Predicate | Matches when |
|---|---|
| `KeyMatch` | source field value equals destination node key (FK) |
| `FieldEqual` | named field is equal on both nodes |
| `Overlap` | Jaccard similarity on list fields exceeds min threshold |
| `NumericWithin` | absolute numeric difference within tolerance |
| `GeoRadius` | Haversine distance on [lat, lon] within km |
| `VectorSimilar` | cosine similarity on float arrays exceeds min |

Predicates compose via `All(...)` (AND, score = min) and `Any(...)` (OR, score = max), nestable to depth 4.

`approximate: true` on `VectorSimilar` uses in-tree HNSW (recall min 0.90, mean 0.998 at 5k/dim 1536, fixed-seed probe).

## Cypher key idiom

Node keys are NOT stored as a property. `n.id` is always null. There is no `key()` function.

- Filter by key: `WHERE n = 'alice'` (node variable equals a string literal)
- Read the key: bare `RETURN n` — the result value for a node variable is the key string

```cypher
MATCH (n:Person) WHERE n = 'alice' RETURN n   -- correct
MATCH (n:Person) WHERE n.id = 'alice' RETURN n -- WRONG: n.id is null
```

In Python, `row["n"]` gives the key string `"alice"`, not a dict.

## Cypher subset

Supported: MATCH, WHERE (AND/OR/NOT, IN, IS NULL/IS NOT NULL), RETURN (DISTINCT), ORDER BY,
SKIP, LIMIT, WITH pipeline, OPTIONAL MATCH, UNWIND, CREATE, MATCH…SET, MATCH…DELETE,
MATCH…DETACH DELETE, MERGE (ON CREATE SET / ON MATCH SET), variable-length paths (*min..max, max 10),
shortestPath, aggregations (COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX, grouped), query parameters ($name),
scalar functions (toLower, toUpper, size, coalesce, type(r), abs, round).

Not supported: CASE, subqueries, UNION, multi-statement BEGIN/COMMIT transactions.

Query result dict keys (Python): the dict keys in each result row are the RETURN aliases
from the query. `RETURN p, o, r.score AS score` produces rows with keys `"p"`, `"o"`, `"score"`.

## Symmetric predicates

When `src_label == dst_label` (e.g., Person-to-Person similarity), the rule fires in both
directions — a property change on any node evaluates that node as both source and destination.
This creates edges in both directions (a→b and b→a). An undirected Cypher pattern
`MATCH (a)-[:SIMILAR]-(b)` double-counts rows. Use directed patterns `MATCH (a)-[:SIMILAR]->(b)`
or `RETURN DISTINCT a, b` to avoid duplicates.

## Node masks and restricted-stub mode

`NodeMask` restricts which nodes are visible to a query. Default behavior (omit mode):
hidden nodes are removed from results entirely — no existence disclosure.

Stub mode (`stub_hidden: true` in HTTP or MCP): hidden nodes appear as
`{"key": "…", "restricted": true}`. Labels, properties, and neighbors are not
disclosed. Use only when your application explicitly needs to indicate a node exists
but is restricted.

- Role tokens **always** use omit mode — `stub_hidden` is silently ignored.
- Cypher result rows are **always omit-only** in both modes.
- Edges to restricted endpoints: in stub mode, the edge object is included with the
  restricted endpoint rendered as `{"key":…,"restricted":true}`; `edge_type` and
  `derived` are present.

HTTP query params: `stub_hidden=true` on `GET /node/{key}`, `GET /node/{key}/edges`,
`GET /node/{key}/neighborhood`. POST /query body field: `"stub_hidden": true`.

## Backup and export

### Backup

- **CLI** (idle store only): `mushroomdb backup <db-dir> <backup-dir>`
- **HTTP** (live-served store): `POST /backup` with body `{"dest": "/path"}`;
  full-token only; read lock held for file copies AND post-copy CRC verification.
  Response: `{"files":[…],"bytes":N,"verified":true}`.
- `backup_to(dest)` Rust API: process-local guarantee only.

### Export

- `mushroomdb export <db-dir> <dest> [--format jsonl|parquet]`
- JSONL: stable, deterministic, byte-identical between runs.
- Parquet: Snappy compression; NOT byte-identical across parquet-rs versions.
- NaN/±Inf `Value::Float` → null in both formats.
- Derived edges include rule attribution (`"rule": "name"`); manual edges: `"rule": null`.

## Full-text search v2 (2026-08-29)

BM25 ranking (k1=1.2, b=0.75) with Snowball English stemming. Query syntax:

| Form | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| `word` | stemmed term |
| `"a b"` | phrase (stemmed adjacency) |
| `-word` | negation (exclude) |
| `word*` | unstemmed prefix |
| `a OR b` | OR groups |

Negation-only queries return empty. Negation-only OR groups contribute nothing to
score. Phrases never match across list-element boundaries. Both index and query paths
use the same stemmer — do not re-stem query tokens.

## Python API notes

`GraphDb.open(path)` creates the database directory if it does not already exist — no
manual mkdir required.

`max_edges` in `create_rule`: Python `None` and a missing key both fill the predicate
default (32 for scored predicates, 1 for KeyMatch). This is the same as HTTP null.
Neither Python nor HTTP can express the Rust `max_edges: None` global-budget hatch
(1,000,000 per source); use the Rust API directly for that.

`query(cypher, params=None)` — `params` accepts a dict or a list of (name, value)
tuples. Values are parameterized, never interpolated — injection-safe regardless of
content. `query_with_params(cypher, params)` is a retained alias.

`rename_node(old_key, new_key)` — rename a node; raises on absent old or duplicate new.

`insert_edge_upsert(edge_type, src_key, dst_key, placeholder_label)` — insert an edge,
auto-creating missing endpoints with `placeholder_label`. Returns
`{"nodes_created": N, "edge_inserted": bool}`.

`query()` result rows are dicts; keys are the RETURN aliases from the Cypher query.

## Temporal history and compare-and-set

Three history APIs expose the WAL timeline with rule attribution:

- `node_history(key)` — every change for a node since the last truncating snapshot
- `edge_history(a, b)` — add/retract lifecycle for all edges between two nodes;
  `rule` field names the rule for derived edges, null for manual edges
- `was_linked(a, b, edge_type, at_commit)` — point-in-time edge existence check

Available over: Rust API, MCP tools (`node_history`, `edge_history`, `was_linked`),
and HTTP (`GET /node/{key}/history`, `GET /history/edge`, `GET /history/was_linked`).

Rule attribution: when the rule engine fires or retracts a derived edge, a
HISTORY-MARKER WAL record (DerivedEdgeAdded discriminant 18, DerivedEdgeRetracted
discriminant 19) is appended in the same commit frame. These markers are state no-ops
on replay (derived edges re-derive from rules deterministically) but are read by
history scans as the authoritative record of when and why each link was created or
retracted.

Horizon contract: all history endpoints return `total_commits` (exclusive upper bound
for valid commit indices). Pre-truncating-snapshot commits are not visible.

Compare-and-set writes (`write_batch_cas` / `submit_batch_cas`): check that nodes
have not changed before committing. `last_changed(key)` returns `Some(commit_seq)` or
`None`. Preconditions are checked atomically; failure → `GraphError::CasConflict`.
`last_changed` values are persisted in V8 snapshot section 11 (LAST_CHANGE).

WAL archives (`archive_wal: true`): renamed WAL segments kept as sidecar files.
Archives always extend history scans (record-scanning is prefix-independent).
Archives extend `open_at` time travel ONLY on an unpruned genesis chain
(wal.genesis present, wal.floor == 0, wal.truncated absent). Pruned or incomplete
genesis chains → CommitOutOfRange for archive-resident commits (never wrong data).

## Storage

- Dense-id WAL with per-commit fsync; configurable FsyncPolicy (strict/batched/relaxed)
- V8 mmap snapshot (v0.2+): 12 rkyv sections (TOPOLOGY, COLUMNS, IDS, SYMS, META,
  EDGE_PROPS, HNSW, PROVENANCE, RULES_META, VIEWS, IVF_STATE, LAST_CHANGE); zero-copy
  open via mmap; no heap allocation for section data; O(1) per-query section access
- V5/V6/V7 snapshots auto-migrated to V8 on open; V3/V4 rejected
- Single writer, many readers (RwLock-backed SharedDb)
- RAM-bound; design target 10M nodes (~5–15 GiB with properties)
- 100k nodes (~10M derived edges), V8 snapshot open: **0.02 s, 31–41 MiB RSS**
  (warm file cache, cold process; measured 2026-08-28, Apple M4 Pro, release build)
- 100k nodes, WAL-only open: ~8.16 min (HNSW re-fitting dominates; measured 2026-08-24)
- V8 snapshot size: 1.8 GiB (same 100k dataset; 18% smaller than V5's 2.2 GiB)
- mushroomdb verify <db-dir>: CRC32 audit of all 12 sections; 0.26 s on 1.8 GiB; exits 2 on mismatch

## Limitations (be honest)

- RAM-bound (mmap is read-only for the snapshot base; in-flight writes are in-memory)
- Single writer (no multi-writer, no clustering, no Neo4j parity)
- No differential dataflow
- Dense patterns >1M intermediate rows require LIMIT
- No multi-statement interactive transactions in v1
- V8 open numbers (0.02 s / 31–41 MiB) are warm-file-cache, cold-process; cold-cache
  numbers not measured (require sudo purge)
- Migration footprint (V5→V8) at 100k nodes: ~30 s, peak ~35 GB VM footprint, ~8.3 GB max RSS (2026-08-28, post-diet); run
  mushroomdb migrate offline on constrained hosts
- Pre-1.0 format policy: snapshot/WAL formats may change between v0.x minor versions
